builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Harnesses That Improve Themselves: A Unifying Framework for Self-Improving Agent Harnesses
summary: This replaces static, manually tuned agent harnesses and prompt-only reflection with a loop that diagnoses execution traces, patches one of four runtime components (context, control, tools, verification), and deploys changes only after validation gates. It costs additional inference for trace diagnosis and patch validation, plus engineering effort to build sandboxed candidate evaluation, though the paper claims lower token cost than full rewrites. It can fail through benchmark gaming, evaluator tampering, prompt bloat, and overfitting of self-modifications to one model or repository.
rationale: Modular, gated harness updates are feasible on a 24 GB GPU or API budget and directly reduce token waste, but the gains are unquantified and must be validated against the reader's own tasks and models.
technique: Self-improving agent harness via gated modular evolution

claims.statement: This replaces static, manually tuned agent harnesses and prompt-only reflection with a loop that diagnoses execution traces, patches one of four runtime components (context, control, tools, verification), and deploys changes only after validation gates. It costs additional inference for trace diagnosis and patch validation, plus engineering effort to build sandboxed candidate evaluation, though the paper claims lower token cost than full rewrites. It can fail through benchmark gaming, evaluator tampering, prompt bloat, and overfitting of self-modifications to one model or repository.
Gated modular harness evolution outperforms prompt reflection and full-harness rewrites on SWE-bench Lite across models and repositories at a fraction of the token cost; no numeric factor is stated.
